title: POC weekly sync - model selection & version pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review recent benchmark results, confirm model selection for the next pilot phase, and finalize version pinning/fallback strategy. Customer reported a few regression cases on longer prompts; Redwood SE proposed pinning to a patched 1.2.1 build with automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant. Action items include running a focused regression eval, updating the benchmark spreadsheet, and sending pricing + pilot SOW.

transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-31
Start Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Park (BrightCart Head of ML), Samir Patel (BrightCart Infra), Rachel Kim (BrightCart PM)

Summary: quick sync on the POC performance and pinning strategy; go over regression cases and agree next steps.

00:00 Alex: hey everybody, thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
00:04 Rachel: yep, loud and clear.
00:08 Alex: great, quick agenda  priya will walk through the latest benchmark runs, then we'll discuss pinning to the 1.2.1 build and fallback options, and finish with next steps.
00:20 Priya: ok, thanks. so we ran the batch of evals you sent last week plus the longer prompt set l-100, and the headline is latency and cost look stable on the dedicated pool but we saw a small regression on the long prompts for the 1.2.0 model variant. accuracy drop is about 3.5% on the completions metric you defined.
00:40 Lena: ok that's the one i was worried about. is that deterministic across seeds or intermittent?
00:45 Priya: mixed  about 70% of cases reproduce locally; some are sensitive to the decoding temp and the prefix cache. the new 1.2.1 patch that our runtime team put together addresses a kv-cache alignment bug which we think is the root cause.
01:05 Samir: sorry quick question, is 1.2.1 already in the catalog on hosted or do we need to ask for a private build?
01:11 Alex: 1.2.1 is available as an experimental variant in the catalog but not the default; for this pilot we can pin you to 1.2.1 on Dedicated or set up a rollout policy that serves 1.2.1 and falls back to the quantized vq-1.0 if cost/latency criteria are hit.
01:28 Rachel: what's the difference with the quantized fallback, how big is the quality delta?
01:33 Priya: the quantized variant vq-1.0 typically shows a small drop  around 4-6% on fine-grained NLU metrics but latency improves by roughly 30%. for many user flows that trade is acceptable; for the specific longer prompts you flagged we'd prefer to keep 1.2.1 pinned.
01:52 Lena: can we do targeted pinning? like pin 1.2.1 for the long-prompt route and let other routes use vq-1.0?
01:59 Alex: absolutely, route-level pinning is the recommended approach. you can pin per API key or per route, and we can couple that with a rollout policy so if error rate increases we auto-rollback to the previous stable version.
02:18 Priya: to add  our rollout engine supports canaries and automatic rollback on metric thresholds (latency, error rate, quality regressions if you feed us the evals). we also support fallback chains, so you can go 1.2.1 -> vq-1.0 -> a lower-cost hosted variant.
02:36 Samir: sounds good. for peering we have tight egress controls. if we go Dedicated we'll need the VPC peering steps and an SOW that calls out network requirements. also want to double check encryption in transit and KMS integration.
02:49 Alex: noted. we'll include the network checklist in the SOW. KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys are supported in Private and Dedicated plans; i'll include options and the SOC2 docs link.
03:04 Lena: one more thing  we saw a couple of hallucination cases with product specs. is that something the model patch can address or is that prompt engineering?
03:12 Priya: a bit of both. some hallucination was due to a tokenization edge-case that 1.2.1 mitigates; others are prompt formulation issues where few-shot context helps. we'll surface examples in the eval report.
03:28 Rachel: could you also flag any latency outliers in the logs? we had a handful over 1.2s which broke our SLOs.
03:35 Priya: yes we'll include a percentile table (p50/p90/p99) and highlight outliers; we captured traces for the offending requests.
03:45 Alex: quick note on billing  if you use route-level pinning with different variants we can roll up costs per route so you can track cost-by-feature in the console.
03:55 Lena: good. do you have a recommended pinning config for our case?
04:00 Priya: recommendation  pin 1.2.1 for long-prompt route with a canary at 10% for two hours, monitor p99 latency and completions quality, rollback to 1.2.0 if quality delta > 2.5% or error rate > 1.5%. set fallback to vq-1.0 after 3x retry failures.
04:23 Samir: are those thresholds adjustable?
04:25 Priya: yes entirely adjustable, we can set them to your tolerances.
04:29 Rachel: timeline-wise, if we agree, when can you pin and run the canary?
04:33 Alex: we can schedule the pin as soon as Monday if you sign off; priya can run the regression eval mid-week and we'll share an updated benchmark.
04:43 Lena: let's aim for Monday for the pin and have the regression report by Wednesday.
04:49 Priya: noted. i'll also add a test harness to reproduce the failing prompts.
04:55 Alex: ok on documentation  we've updated the benchmark spreadsheet here: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/brightcart-poc (link)  i'll share a copy with edit access.
05:07 Lena: perfect. on security, Samir will send the contact for compliance and we'll need SOC2 + iso docs.
05:12 Samir: i'll email that after the call.
05:16 Alex: great. quick recap of action items and owners then close.
05:21 Rachel: thanks everyone.
